subsenses.definition: (physics) Matter made up of normal particles, not antiparticles.
Printed material, especially in books or magazines.
examples: He always took some reading matter with him on the plane.

subsenses.definition: (philosophy) Aristotelian: undeveloped potentiality subject to change and development; formlessness. Matter receives form, and becomes substance.

senses.definition: An affair, condition, or subject, especially one of concern or (especially when preceded by the) one that is problematic.
examples: Something is the matter with him.
The diplomats met to discuss state matters.
